scope: Five focused real-account scenarios plus explicit cross-node logout and recovery rechecks; broader A01–A13 release acceptance remains open.

focusedRun.environment: real isolated IAM, 2 Auth, 2 BFF, Gateway, shared MySQL/Redis

cases.name: A→B→A real browser and native peer synchronization
two real tabs commit competing transactions on different BFF nodes
peer browser logout while real Auth issuance result is in flight (round-robin topology)
dropped successful commit response restores exactly the original result (round-robin topology)
real clock reaches original login deadline after continuous switches

focusedRun.sourceWorkingTrees: Uncommitted implementation in both repositories; deployed fatJar hashes identify the tested backend packages.
limits: Two Auth and two BFF JVMs on one host with a shared single Redis/MySQL; no claim of Redis cluster or cross-host partition testing.
Native UI/peer synchronization is verified in round trip; deterministic CAS competition uses real authenticated requests queued from two browser tabs, followed by page revalidation.
The public BFF client issues no Refresh Token. This run verifies BFF/Cookie/Access Token absolute cutoff; it does not claim a real refresh-token flow.

Only the five focused scenarios are closed. Original membership loss, restricted menus, dependency outages, audit-center persistence, customer CA and coordinated release/rollback remain separate acceptance items.

findingsFixed: F03: restored BFF YAML account/event/BFF nesting and removed duplicate root keys in all environments.
F04: distinguished server-side pre-authorization credential admission from direct password grant; missing authenticated client now returns invalid_client instead of 500.
F05: formal session Cookie uses fixed UTC HTTP Expires and no positive Max-Age, preserving original cutoff on delivery and resume.
notes: The initial round-robin run happened to use the same BFF node for logout and for result resume. Cross-node assertions are backed by the separate explicitly routed supplement; raw request metadata is preserved.

Cookie wire Expires equals the original deadline exactly. Chromium exposes a fractional local Cookie-expiry estimate; protocol values, actual server expiry and explicit expired-Cookie replay are verified separately.
Unused issuance after logout stays in the durable cleanup ledger, bounded by the source deadline; this is not a claim of immediate revocation or pre-deadline ledger drainage.
